subject: circuits

milestone.title: RC time constant
milestone.objective: Compute the time constant of an RC circuit and the capacitor voltage after 1 to 5 time constants

sources.title: EE notes: RC circuits (fixture)
sources.text: When a capacitor C charges through a resistor R from a DC source, the time constant is tau = R C (seconds, with R in ohms and C in farads). After one time constant the capacitor voltage reaches about 63.2 % of its final value. After 5 time constants it reaches about 99.3 %, and the capacitor is usually considered fully charged. When discharging, the voltage falls to about 36.8 % of its starting value after one time constant. Example: R = 10 kilohm and C = 100 microfarad give tau = 10,000 x 0.0001 = 1 s.

lesson_lines: A capacitor C charging through a resistor R has time constant **τ = R C**. With R in ohms and C in farads, τ is in seconds.
- After 1 τ, the capacitor reaches about **63.2 %** of its final voltage.
- After 5 τ, about **99.3 %**: treat it as fully charged.
- Discharging, the voltage falls to about **36.8 %** of its starting value after 1 τ.
R = 4.7 kΩ, C = 220 µF, charged from 9 V. Find τ and the capacitor voltage after 1 τ.
